topics.title: Descriptive Statistics
topics.description: Summarizing and describing data using measures of center, spread, and shape.
objectives: Calculate variance, standard deviation, and IQR
Interpret histograms, boxplots, and scatter plots

problem_templates.prompt_template: Given the dataset [4, 7, 13, 2, 7, 9, 1, 14, 7, 6], compute the mean, median, mode, variance, and standard deviation. Show all steps.
For the dataset [2, 5, 8, 12, 15, 18, 22, 25], construct a boxplot. Identify Q1, Q3, IQR, and any outliers using the 1.5×IQR rule.

Two datasets have the same mean of 50. Dataset A has standard deviation 5; Dataset B has standard deviation 20. Explain what this reveals about their distributions and sketch the expected shape of each histogram.

topics.title: Probability
topics.description: Fundamental rules of probability, conditional probability, and independence.
objectives: Define probability using set theory and sample spaces
Compute conditional probability and use Bayes' theorem

problem_templates.prompt_template: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn without replacement. Find P(both red), P(one of each), and P(both blue). Use the multiplication rule.

A disease affects 1% of the population. A test has 95% sensitivity and 90% specificity. Given a positive test result, what is the probability the patient has the disease? Apply Bayes' theorem and explain the base-rate fallacy.
Two events A and B have P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.3, P(A∩B) = 0.1. Compute P(A|B), P(B|A), P(A∪B). Are A and B independent? Prove your answer using the definition.

topics.title: Probability Distributions
topics.description: Discrete and continuous distributions — binomial, Poisson, normal, and more.
objectives: Work with binomial and Poisson distributions
Understand the normal distribution and standardization

problem_templates.prompt_template: A fair coin is flipped 10 times. Using the binomial distribution, find P(exactly 6 heads), P(at least 8 heads), and E[heads]. Show the PMF formula.
Test scores are normally distributed with μ = 72, σ = 10. Find (a) P(score > 85), (b) P(60 < score < 80), (c) the 90th percentile. Use z-scores and the standard normal table.

A factory produces 200 items/hour with each item defective with probability 0.02. Compare the exact Poisson approximation to the binomial for P(≥5 defects/hour). Explain when the approximation is valid.

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing
topics.description: Statistical inference framework for testing claims about population parameters.
objectives: Understand Type I and Type II errors
Apply t-tests, z-tests, and chi-square tests

problem_templates.prompt_template: A sample of 30 students has mean exam score 78 with s = 12. Test H₀: μ = 75 vs H₁: μ > 75 at α = 0.05. State the t-statistic, degrees of freedom, and conclusion.
Explain the relationship between p-value, significance level α, and Type I error. Give an example where a p-value of 0.03 would lead to different conclusions at α = 0.01 vs α = 0.05.

A chi-square test for independence: a survey of 200 people records gender (M/F) and preference (A/B/C). Given a contingency table, test independence at α = 0.05. Compute expected frequencies, the chi-square statistic, and state the conclusion.

topics.title: Regression Analysis
topics.description: Modeling relationships between variables — simple and multiple linear regression.
objectives: Fit a simple linear regression model

problem_templates.prompt_template: Given data points (1,2), (2,4), (3,5), (4,4), (5,5), derive the least-squares regression line ŷ = a + bx by computing b = Σ(xᵢ−x̄)(yᵢ−ȳ)/Σ(xᵢ−x̄)². Predict y at x = 6.
For a regression model with R² = 0.72, interpret what this means. Describe each of the four key assumptions of linear regression and explain how to check each with a residual plot.
Distinguish between correlation and causation using a concrete example. Explain Simpson's paradox and construct a small dataset that demonstrates it.

topics.title: Bayesian Inference
topics.description: Updating beliefs with evidence using Bayes' theorem as a general inference framework.
objectives: Apply Bayes' theorem to update distributions

problem_templates.prompt_template: You have a coin whose fairness is unknown. You flip it 5 times and get 4 heads. Start with a uniform prior on p ∈ [0,1], state the likelihood function for Binomial(5, p), and describe (without computing) the posterior distribution.
Using a Beta(2,2) prior for a coin's probability of heads, observe 7 heads in 10 flips. Write the posterior distribution, compute its mean and mode, and compare to the MLE estimate.
Explain the key philosophical difference between a Bayesian credible interval and a frequentist confidence interval. Construct an example where they give different numerical answers.
